entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv4669"/><div sID="gen6767" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv4669"/>22. The ideas of order and light, disorder and darkness, harmonize (<reference osisRef="Gen.1.2">Ge 1:2</reference>). Three Hebrew words are used for darkness; in <reference osisRef="Job.10.21">Job 10:21</reference> (<reference osisRef="1Cor.10.1">1</reference>) the common word "darkness"; here (2) "a land of gloom" (from a Hebrew root, "to cover up"); (3) as "thick darkness" or blackness (from a root, expressing sunset). "Where the light thereof is like blackness." Its only sunshine is thick darkness. A bold figure of poetry. Job in a better frame has brighter thoughts of the unseen world. But his views at best wanted the definite clearness of the Christian's. Compare with his words here <reference osisRef="Rev.21.23">Re 21:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.5">22:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Tim.1.10">2Ti 1:10</reference>. <chapter eID="Job.10"/>
entries.content_plain: 22. The ideas of order and light, disorder and darkness, harmonize ( Ge 1:2 ). "Where the light thereof is like blackness." Its only sunshine is thick darkness. A bold figure of poetry. Job in a better frame has brighter thoughts of the unseen world. But his views at best wanted the definite clearness of the Christian's. Compare with his words here Re 21:23 ; 22:5 ; 2Ti 1:10 .
